rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 is the best verified design (374.39). Its raced design is body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 m and y = 0.05 m, with kp 2.0, ki 0.5, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.3 and line_loss 'search_left'. It finished 20 of 20 oval runs (mean progress 0.998, mean time 1.88 s). Its s-bend (progress 0.318) and slalom (progress 0.103) still leave the tape, with about 1 line-loss event per run.

What I kept: the iteration-10 design exactly. Every controller and geometry value matches a raced run, so the expected score is about 374 on the development tracks. The final unseen track is the only place where this design is untested, and a verified baseline is the safest choice for that race.

What I rejected from the draft: (a) The draft's geometry (8 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016 m, y = 0.06 m, body 0.12 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, track 0.10 m) has never raced with a verified result. Iteration 9's reproduction of 344.50 showed that edits to that geometry are not confirmed in the race, so I do not build on it. (b) The draft's base_speed 1.1 is an extrapolation. Iteration 10 ran at 1.3, and the draft's claim that 'base_speed 1.2 was the best run' does not match the record. The speed evidence is 1.5 to 1.3 (score 344.5 to 374.4, with oval finishes rising from 17 to 20 of 20). No run exists at 1.1, and the draft's time and completion estimates for it are unsupported. (c) kd 0.6 and ki 0.1 were drawn from the unverified geometry. ki 0.5 and search_left are the controller settings that produced the verified gains, so I keep them.

Critique points accepted: the critique is right that the draft's expected s-bend and slalom gains have no basis, and that its time-term cost was understated. I do not claim bend progress will rise. I also accept that the line-loss phase is untested, but I do not test it here, because a change to line_loss could cost the oval completions that carry most of the verified score. I rejected the critique's suggestion to try base_speed 1.2 on this geometry: it is a single-variable test that could only lower the final-race score if it fails, and this is the final iteration.

Expected result: oval completion at or near 0.95 to 1.0, mean finish time about 1.9 s, s-bend progress about 0.32 and slalom about 0.10, consistent with the iteration-10 record.
